content: This medication, known as cefaclor, is a cephalosporin-type antibiotic used to treat a variety of bacterial infections, including those affecting the middle ear, skin, urinary tract, and respiratory tract. It is important to note that this antibiotic is only effective against bacterial infections and will not work for viral infections such as the common cold or flu. Before using cefaclor, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to penicillins, or to other cephalosporins. Additionally, disclose any other allergies you may have, as this product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other complications. Cefaclor may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary, as it passes into breast milk. Shake the bottle well before each dose. Take this medication orally, with or without food, as directed by your doctor, typically every 8 or 12 hours. For optimal results, take the antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals and continue the full prescribed course, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Common side effects may include stomach upset, headache, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. While this medication is prescribed because the benefits outweigh the risks, it may rarely cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition can occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of cefaclor may lead to oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Cefaclor may interfere with certain lab tests, such as some diabetic urine tests, potentially causing false results. If someone overdoses and experiences severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center immediately. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication in the refrigerator and do not freeze it. Discard any unused portion after 14 days. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
